# Product Architecture Store

The product's standing architecture, in one home: `.mochiko/product/architecture/`. Two layers
ride together — a topology SPINE (containers, boundaries, communication styles) and a CONCERN
CATALOG (AX-XXX rows: auth, tenancy, billing, observability, ...). A concern row may pin to a
spine element or apply product-wide. Every element carries a lifecycle status, so intent and
built state live on one surface.

Authored and amended per mochiko:authoring-architecture-store — the skill carries the write
timing, the lifecycle rules, the landing duties, and the drift discipline; this shape carries
only the structure. Stances are formed per mochiko:patterns-architecture-shelves.

The sections below map to the PARTS OF A MULTI-FILE ARTIFACT — the store's own files — not to
sections of a single document. That is a deliberate fit for a directory-shaped artifact, not
altitude drift.

Shape principle: a SMALL REQUIRED CORE plus broad flexibility. The required core is element ids,
status values, stance values, and pointer fields — nothing else. Beyond it everything is legal:
extra fields, extra sections, local diagrams, long-form prose. The schema constrains the
skeleton, never the voice.

The `--check` view grades the SKELETON ONLY — required core fields present, status and stance
values legal, ids unique, `Work:`/NFR pointers resolving — and never the free-form body. It is
an advisory view, never a gate.

## Store layout

The store is four files, three of them written by hand and one derived:

| File | Holds |
|------|-------|
| `.mochiko/product/architecture/spine.md` | the topology deep view |
| `.mochiko/product/architecture/concerns.md` | the AX-XXX concern ledger |
| `.mochiko/product/architecture/concerns/AX-XXX-<slug>.md` | a graduated concern's deep view (only where one exists) |
| `ARCHITECTURE.md` (repo root) | the DERIVED index — regenerated on every store write, never hand-maintained |

The root index stays at the repo root, never inside the store directory. A store may exist
with no graduated concern files at all; that is the normal starting state.

## Spine

`spine.md` — the topology deep view. Carries the container diagram, an element table, and
sequence diagrams for qualifying flows (diagram craft and altitude: mochiko:patterns-system-design).

The header carries a `Scope:` line naming the surface types the store covers — e.g.
`Scope: backend-service`, or several for a full-stack product. Setup's scaffold writes it;
the desk may override it. This is the durable home of shelf scope.

REQUIRED CORE, per spine element: an id `SPN-XXX` (unique across the store), a `kind`
(`container` | `boundary` | `flow`), a name, and a lifecycle `status`. Everything else —
responsibility text, communication style, technology notes, local diagrams — is free-form.

Legal `status` values (the same set governs concern rows):
`ruled` · `in-flight (FEAT-XXX)` · `modifying (FEAT-XXX)` · `removing (FEAT-XXX)` · `built`.
The three middle values MUST carry their FEAT-XXX key; `ruled` and `built` MUST NOT.

Status tracks the BUILD lifecycle and is independent of stance. `ruled` is the resting
status of any element not in flight and not yet built — including a concern row whose
stance is `open` or `n-a`. Do not read `ruled` as "a stance was decided".

## Concern ledger (AX rows)

`concerns.md` — one entry per concern, compact by default. Rows start here and graduate to
their own file only on real depth.

REQUIRED CORE, per row: an id `AX-XXX` (unique across the store), a concern name, a
`Stance`, and a lifecycle `Status` (same value set as spine elements).

Four stances: `decided` · `not-now` · `n-a` · `open` — `n-a` is never written bare (below).
Two carry an obligation:
  - `not-now` — an `Upgrade trigger` line is expected (the deferral's revisit condition);
  - `n-a` — a reason axis is REQUIRED, either `genuinely never` or `handled elsewhere`.

The reason axis is written as a SUFFIX ON THE STANCE. An `n-a` row's stance therefore reads
in full as `n-a — genuinely never` or `n-a — handled elsewhere`, and both suffixed forms
are legal stance values everywhere a stance is written — ledger row, graduated file, and
the derived index table alike. A bare `n-a` carrying its reason somewhere else is not
legal. `n-a — handled elsewhere` MUST also carry its pointer to the system that owns the
concern; that pointer's home is the `Owned by` field.

What a stance MEANS, and what may constrain the choice, is not this shape's business —
see mochiko:patterns-architecture-shelves.

Conventional free-form fields, present where they carry something: `Ruling` (+ ruled date),
`Rationale`, `Upgrade trigger`, `Owned by` (the handled-elsewhere pointer's home — required
on an `n-a — handled elsewhere` row, absent otherwise), `Targets` (NFR-XXX ids with their
measurable target, measurement method, and source — the FR-XXX / SC-XXX whose promise the
target serves — live HERE, one home per concern), `As-built`, `Drift`, `Work` (FEAT-XXX / EPIC-XXX pointers;
the work itself lives on the feature map, never here).

Every `Work:`, NFR-XXX, and `handled elsewhere` pointer MUST resolve. A dangling pointer is
a defect, not a placeholder.

## Graduated concern file — optional

`.mochiko/product/architecture/concerns/AX-XXX-<slug>.md` — present ONLY for a row that
earned its own file: long rationale, local diagrams, a decision trail the ledger cannot
hold in a few lines. Extend beats mint; a row that fits the ledger stays in the ledger.

A graduated file carries the same required core as its ledger row (id, name, stance,
status) and then whatever depth the concern actually has. The ledger keeps the row with a
one-line summary and a link — the row never disappears from the ledger when it graduates.

## Derived root index

`ARCHITECTURE.md` at the repo root — a rendered VIEW of the store, regenerated on every
store write by its single writer. Never hand-edited; index-vs-store disagreement is a
defect fixed on sight, never reconciled by editing the index.

Three parts:
  1. Spine thumbnail — the container view at a glance, plus a link to `spine.md`.
  2. AX summary table — one line per concern row (`AX-XXX` · concern · stance · status ·
     one-line summary · link). This is the full row set, not a selection: it is the surface
     the sufficiency check and the design phase read, so a missing row is an invisible row.
  3. Health — the health view, a SECTION OF THIS INDEX and not a separate artifact. Five
     counts, each naming its rows: open rows · stale `not-now` triggers · fired triggers
     awaiting routing · orphan elements (an in-flight-class element whose FEAT-XXX is not
     an open feature) · drift register.

The index carries no content of its own: everything in it is derived from the store.

# Concern Ledger

## AX-001 Tenancy

- **Stance**: decided
- **Status**: built
- **Ruling**: pooled multi-tenant, `tenant_id` row-level scoping (ruled [DATE])
- **Rationale**: [why this, and what it costs]
- **Upgrade trigger**: first enterprise deal requiring silo OR >[N] tenants
- **Targets**: NFR-014 (from SC-007) — tenant-scoped read p95 < 200ms, measured at the API gateway histogram
- **As-built**: pooled; `tenant_id` on 14 tables
- **Drift**: none
- **Work**: FEAT-012, EPIC-004

## AX-002 SSO

- **Stance**: not-now
- **Status**: ruled
- **Rationale**: [real concern, consciously deferred — why now is not the time]
- **Upgrade trigger**: first prospect whose security review demands SAML

## AX-003 Payments ledger

- **Stance**: n-a — handled elsewhere
- **Status**: ruled
- **Owned by**: [system/repo that owns this concern]   <!-- pointer REQUIRED on handled-elsewhere -->

## AX-004 Experimentation

- **Stance**: open
- **Status**: ruled
- **Note**: [walked, no stance formed yet — counted by the health view]
